stages.answer_line: (RECOMMENDED OPENING DEFINITION): “Sāṃkhya (the enumerative dualist school) is a realist dualism in which three pramāṇas (means of valid knowledge) establish one unconscious Prakṛti (primordial material nature) and many conscious Puruṣas (pure witnesses).”.

EVOLUTES NEED AN UNEVOLVED GROUND PLEASURE/PAIN/DULLNESS IN EFFECTS
NOT “MATTER” ALONE, BUT PSYCHOPHYSICAL SOURCE OF INTELLECT, SENSES

PRAKṚTI: beginningless, unmanifest, independent material cause
not “matter” alone, but psychophysical source of intellect, senses and elements.

stages.answer_line: (RECOMMENDED OPENING DEFINITION): “Puruṣa (the pure conscious witness) is inactive, non-objectifiable and distinct from every product of Prakṛti, while jīva (the empirical embodied self) is Puruṣa apparently identified with intellect, ego and the subtle body.”.

stages.answer_line: (CORE ARGUMENT): “Satkāryavāda (the theory that the effect pre-exists potentially in its cause) and pariṇāmavāda (real transformation) make the evolution of twenty-five fundamental principles a manifestation of determinate causal powers rather than creation from non-being.”.

stages.title: SATKĀRYAVĀDA

pills.text: EFFECT PRE-EXISTS LATENTLY IN CAUSE ASADAKARAṆĀT
SPECIFIC MATERIAL CAUSE IS SELECTED SARVASAMBHAVĀBHĀVĀT
NOT EVERYTHING ARISES FROM EVERYTHING ŚAKTASYA ŚAKYAKARAṆĀT
CAUSE PRODUCES ONLY WHAT IT HAS POWER TO PRODUCE
EFFECT SHARES NATURE OF CAUSE PARIṆĀMAVĀDA

sequence: EFFECT PRE-EXISTS LATENTLY IN CAUSE asadakaraṇāt: non-being cannot be produced upādānagrahaṇāt: specific material cause is
everything arises from everything śaktasya śakyakaraṇāt: cause produces only what it has power to produce
nature of cause pariṇāmavāda: real transformation of prakṛti
NYĀYA ārambhavāda: new effect
ADVAITA vivarta: apparent transformation.

stages.answer_line: (FINAL VERDICT): “The power of Sāṃkhya (the enumerative dualist school) lies in connecting epistemology, material continuity, empirical consciousness and liberation within one system; its weakness is that the relation required to connect its two absolutes remains under-explained.”.

stages.title: WHY MANY PURUṢAS?

pills.text: PURUṢA EXISTS BECAUSE COMPOSITES SERVE ANOTHER
EXPERIENCE NEEDS CONSCIOUS WITNESS OBJECTS OF THREE GUṆAS REQUIRE
BIRTHS/DEATHS DIFFER; SENSE CAPACITIES AND ACTIONS ARE UNCOORDINATED
IF ONE PURUṢA, ONE PERSON'S LIBERATION OR PAIN WOULD
INACTIVE CONSCIOUSNESS CANNOT LITERALLY TOUCH UNCONSCIOUS PRAKṚTI ANALOGIES

sequence: PURUṢA EXISTS BECAUSE composites serve another
experience needs conscious witness objects of three guṇas require non-guṇa experiencer
liberation is conceivable
PLURALITY: births/deaths differ; sense capacities and actions are uncoordinated
if one puruṣa, one person's liberation or pain would belong to all

stages.answer_line: (CRITICISM): “Sāṃkhya (the enumerative dualist school) integrates psychology, cosmology and liberation without a creator God, yet guṇa-explanation risks elasticity, Puruṣa-plurality lacks a clear individuator, and mere proximity does not fully solve the contact problem.”.

TELEOLOGY IS IMMANENT, AS MILK FLOWS FOR CALF; NO

LAYER 3 - ADVANCED Advanced proof burden and cognition model Samkhya reduces comparison, postulation, non-apprehension and tradition to

groups.heading: ADVANCED OBJECTION
items: its three accepted pramanas.
This economy creates a burden: imperceptible Prakriti and Purusa cannot simply be asserted.
Samanyato-drsta inference must reach entities never presented as ordinary sense-objects.
Carvaka attacks the unobserved universal relation, while Nyaya grants inference but proposes atoms and Isvara as a more economical explanation.

groups.heading: COMPARATIVE NUANCE
items: Samkhya replies that material continuity, guna-patterns and the objectifiability of experience jointly require one material root and a
distinct witness.
Empirical cognition occurs through the inner instrument.
Manas coordinates, ahamkara appropriates and buddhi determines.
